newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Pacific to close plant, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Pacific to close plant, take charge.

text.p: Louisiana-Pacific Corp Monday said it will take a $350 million pre-tax charge in the third quarter to reflect the shutdown of its Ketchikan Pulp Co subsidiary's pulp mill and other items.
In a statement, the company said the charge totals $215 million after taxes or $2.00 per share.

In addition to the plant closing, the company said the charge covers the settlement of all outstanding shareholder securities class action claims, a reserve for other litigation, and a reserve for the planned fourth quarter shutdown and other costs related to certain other non-strategic facilities.

Chairman and Chief Executive Mark Suwyn, attributed the shutdown to the "failure to reach a satisfactory agreement with the Clinton Administration to restore the original terms of KPC's timber supply contract."

The company said unilateral changes to the contract by the U.S. Forest Service in 1991 led to "significant operating losses for the mill." The portion of the reserve related to the closure is $188 million. Through the first nine months of this year, the pulp operations lost an estimated $40 million.

Louisiana Pacific said Ketchikan Pulp will enter into immediate negotiations with the Department of Agriculture to determine the feasibility of continuing to run its two sawmills in southeast Alaska for two more years.

Louisiana-Pacific also said it has agreed in principle to settle, on behalf of all defendants, all outstanding shareholder securities class action claims brought against the company and four of its former and current officers last year.

The suits currently are pending in the federal court in Portland, Oregon and stem from a drop in Louisiana Pacific's stock price following media and analyst accounts on May 25, 1995 of certain threatened or pending civil and criminal actions against the company.
The defendants agreed to the settlement without admitting any liability.
The company said the settlement calls for a payment of $65 million, of which approximately $20 million will be covered by insurance.
The after-tax cost of the uninsured portion is approximately $28 million, or $.26 per share, which will be accrued in the third quarter of 1996.

In addition, the company said it intends to reserve an additional $117 million in the third quarter for anticipated costs associated with other outstanding litigation and claims, and for anticipated costs of shutting down and disposing of certain non-essential plants and equipment.

"During the fourth quarter we plan to announce the closing or sale of several plants which are no longer competitive or essential to our future operations," the company said. "Our goal is to adjust our capacity to meet what we believe will be the future demand for our current products. A final announcement on exactly which plants will be closed will be made in the next 30-60 days."
The company said the target date for the shutdown is March 24, 1997. About 500 employees are expected to be affected by the shutdown.
